$title: Chavost Blanc d'Assemblage Brut Nature Champagne 750ml
$description: 50% Chardonnay, 50% Pinot Meunier Soil is limestone clay and chalk blended, North facing No added SO2 Spontaneous yeasts 4 months aging in stainless steel, 20 months in bottle 750ml bottle
3_second_reach: Chavost — a 70-grower Champagne co-op that went fully organic under fourth-generation winemaker Fabien Daviaux. Zero sulphur added.

$title: André Heucq 'Héritage Assemblage' Extra Brut, NV, 375ml
$description: Winery: Fourth-generation family grower-producer (récoltant-manipulant) in Cuisles, Vallée de la Marne — not a négociant house buying grapes, they farm their own ~6 hectares. Founded 1936 by the original André Heucq, expanded by son Roger in 1955, and shaped into its current organic/biodynamic identity by the current André starting in 1973; his daughter Fanny now works alongside him. The estate sits on a rare soil type called "green illite," a clay not found elsewhere in Champagne, which Peter Liem singles out in his book Champagne as ideal Meunier country — fitting, since 80% of the estate's total plantings are Pinot Meunier, a grape most big Champagne houses treat as a filler variety. Winemaking: Direct press, native yeast, fermented partly in oak (30%) and partly stainless (70%), then aged a substantial 60 months on lees before disgorgement. Dosage is just 1.8 g/l — essentially bone dry, on the austere end even for "Extra Brut." Sulfites kept low, 15–20 mg/L. (40% Chardonnay, 30% Meunier, 30% Pinot Noir) Tasting notes: Deep golden color, fine persistent bead. Nose of white fruits, fresh-baked bread, honey, white pepper, and herbal tea — the extended lees aging and low dosage show through as bready, savory complexity rather than fruit-forward sweetness. Food pairings: Oysters, aged Comté or Gruyère, roast chicken, sushi, salted almonds — the bready richness and bone-dry finish want something savory, not dessert.
3_second_reach: André Heucq — four generations farming a clay called 'green illite' found nowhere else in Champagne, plowing by horse since before biodynamics was fashionable.

$description: Ripe pear, crisp green apple, and hints of flower blossoms on the nose, with nuanced minerality that brings elegance and bright tension to the palate.
3_second_reach: Jacques Dumont — a small Loire grower whose Vouvray gets its honeyed edge from tuffeau, the chalky limestone under every great Chenin Blanc site.

$title: Zind Humbrecht Riesling Roche Granitique Alsace 750ml
$description: TASTING NOTE Yellow bright colour. The nose shows a crystalline purity, some citrus fruits, but mostly dominated by the granitic rock that gives a strong precise mineral feel and an almost light reductive profile. No doubt that this wine will benefit from decanting in its youth. The palate is elegant and suave. Immediately elegant and digest, the granite is able to hide the intensity and powerful texture. Medium acidity compensated by interesting minerals and ripe saline elements. The finish is dry but so expressive. Another 2022 that is showing well today and will also in the distant future.
3_second_reach: Zind-Humbrecht — Olivier Humbrecht, one of Alsace's most decorated biodynamic producers. Roche Granitique names the granite bedrock doing the work here.

$title: Le Mistral Joseph's Red Blend Monterey 2019 750ml
$description: Joseph Phelps created the Le Mistral Vineyard and label in 1985 as part of his "Rhône Ranger" project (he'd already made California's first varietal Syrah in 1974). Phelps sold the Le Mistral brand and 40-acre Arroyo Seco vineyard to Ventana Vineyards in 2007 (confirmed via Wine Spectator), and it later passed to Folktale Winery under Gregory Ahn. "Joseph's Blend" is literally named in tribute to Phelps. 2019 composition: 48% Grenache, 39% Syrah, 13% Mourvèdre (this blend shifts by vintage — 2017 was 64/33/3 Grenache-Syrah-Petite Sirah, 2021 was 61/39 Grenache-Syrah — so vintage-to-vintage variation is part of the story, not a flaw). Tasting notes (Wine Enthusiast, Matt Kettmann): fresh boysenberry, violet, and dusty-rock aromas; boysenberry and black-plum on the palate riding through "rocky fields of lavender." Aged roughly 11 months in French oak, single-vineyard, ~900+ cases produced, quoted aging potential of 10-12 years. Food pairings: Lamb, herb-roasted or grilled chicken, mushroom dishes, hard aged cheeses — classic GSM territory.
3_second_reach: Le Mistral Joseph's Blend — the Rhône wine Joseph Phelps built his reputation on, named for him after he sold it, still made from the same 40-acre Arroyo Seco vineyard.

$description: San Juan, where Jelu Estate is based, is around 100 miles north of Mendoza. The company was established there in 2002. Duncan Killiner, the company's co-founder and winemaker, frequently discusses the unique environment of the Zonda Valley. When Duncan was in his twenties, he became known as a "flying winemaker," consulting for vineyards all around the globe. During that time, they worked 80 harvests. He stopped in Uruguay for a while before taking a position in Mendoza, Argentina, in 2002. After working there for six months, he saw Argentina for what it was truly capable of. Duncan gets his grapes from places like San Juan's Zonda Valley and Patagonia, both of which practice organic farming methods. January (the southern hemisphere's equivalent of July) is grape harvest time, which is earlier than the norm for the region. Duncan does this so that the wines end up with just the right amount of acidity and alcohol after fermentation is complete. Duncan's passion for winemaking and the San Juan region's natural beauty come through in the vibrant, vivacious wines made in the high-elevation glacial valley.
3_second_reach: Jelu — a New Zealand winemaker chasing Malbec in Argentina's Zonda Valley, where the temperature swings 50 degrees in a single day. That's where this color comes from.

$description: Family estate in Monforte d'Alba, right in the heart of the Bussia cru. Carlo Ghisolfi bought into Bussia in 1985; his son Attilio expanded the holdings; grandson Gianmarco has run the winery since 1988 and is now into a fifth generation of family winemaking. About 17 acres total, mostly Nebbiolo with some Barbera and Freisa. Tasting notes: Ruby-red to garnet, flowery and expansive on the nose, well-balanced, deep, tannic, long finish — drinkable young for a Barolo but built to age. Three major critics weighed in on this exact vintage: Wine Spectator (95 pts) found "rose, cherry, licorice, tobacco, cut hay and tar," calling it "solidly built" with a drinking window of 2024–2043. James Suckling (94 pts) called it clear and refined with dark-berry and candied-citrus notes, medium-bodied, tight fine tannins. Wine Enthusiast (94 pts) found camphor, forest floor, blue flowers, ripe Morello cherry and star anise, suggesting 2027–2032. Sourced from south/southwest-facing vineyards 5–18 years old on marly white tufa soil, native-yeast fermentation, 10-day maceration, aged 36 months in large Slavonian oak plus 6 months in bottle. Food pairings: Roasts, game, truffle dishes, mature cheeses — straight from the winery's own notes.
3_second_reach: Attilio Ghisolfi — a family that's worked the Bussia cru since 1985, farming organically without ever bothering to get certified. Bussia is loved by many!

$title: Le Mistral Cabernet Sauvignon Paso Robles 2021 750ml
$description: Produced by Folktale Wine Group (Carmel, CA / Monterey County), founded by Greg & Madigan Ahn. Le Mistral has a bit of pedigree — the label originated under Joseph Phelps, passed to the Brosseau family, and now lives at Folktale. This Cab specifically is sourced from Royal Estrella Vineyard in Paso Robles, farmed by Don Brady and Randy Johnston — a vineyard with a brutal diurnal swing (100°F+ days, down to 50°F at night) that's the whole reason for the concentration in the glass. Tasting notes: Plum and dried cherry, long bold finish, big ripe fruit and tannin structure with refreshing acidity from that day/night temperature swing. Hand-harvested pre-dawn, native fermentation, daily hand punch-downs, aged in French oak, bottled ~10 months later. Food pairings: Steak, lamb, hearty pasta — a Cab built for the grill, not delicate food.
3_second_reach: Le Mistral — Joseph Phelps' old Central Coast label, still sourcing Cabernet from Paso's Royal Estrella Vineyard under new ownership at Folktale.

$description: William Downie started his label in 2003 after training at Bass Phillip (under the legendary Phillip Jones) and later became senior winemaker at De Bortoli. He also did harvests in Burgundy with Domaines Fourrier and Hubert Lignier — when Romain Lignier died unexpectedly in 2004, Downie was brought in to lead winemaking there for two vintages. He's since narrowed his own-vineyard focus to Gippsland exclusively, growing nothing but Pinot Noir. Cathedral is named for Little Cathedral Farm, one of its component vineyards, planted in 1998 at the foot of Victoria's Cathedral Range on 400-million-year-old sandstone and shale — that's genuinely where the name comes from, nothing to do with Gippsland. Winemaking: Fully hands-off — destemmed but not crushed, native-yeast fermentation in wood and stainless with no temperature control, no punch-downs or pump-overs, no additions beyond a small SO2 dose before bottling, aged in stainless (no oak). 13% ABV, Stelvin screwcap. Tasting notes: Medium ruby with a garnet edge. Lifted, wild aromatics — native berries (lilly pilly, muntries), bush tomato, pickled rosella, mace, anise myrtle — plus red cherry, wild strawberry, raspberry, rose petal and violet. Palate is light, juicy, fruit-forward with silky tannins: raspberry, cranberry, pomegranate, delicate spice, pink pepper on the finish. Food pairings: Duck, mushroom dishes, charcuterie, or lightly seared salmon — the wine's light body and high aromatics want something delicate, not a heavy roast.
3_second_reach: William Downie — Australia's minimal-intervention Pinot pioneer out of Gippsland. Cathedral is proof great Pinot doesn't need a big price tag.

$title: La Rivolta I Vigneti di Bruma Aglianico Beneventano IGT 2021 750ml
$description: A medium to full-bodied red wine made from a local variety and aged in stainless steel. Rich and intense, with notes of red fruits, particularly sour cherry. Slightly earthy with good structure.
3_second_reach: La Rivolta — Campania's Sannio hills, where locals call Aglianico 'the Barolo of the South' for its grip and its patience.

$title: Duval Leroy Femme Brut Grand Cru Champagne 750ml
$description: TASTING NOTES Its golden yellow color bears fine lines of bubbles that reveal complex notes of lively maturity: brioche, vanilla and woody aromas alternating with citrus fruit such as lemon and mandarin. A fine attack of mouth is followed by a silky touch with infinite persistence. A family business and a French institution, their House has dedicated itself to the noble craft of champagne-making since 1859. Champagne pioneers, Duval-Leroy has always been driven by a quest for high standards and innovation in every aspect of the business, from quality, consistency and certification through to partnerships with sommeliers and chefs.Following in the footsteps of Carol, our “lady of champagne”, her three sons Julien, Charles and Louis have now come on board to perpetuate the house spirit.Four individuals now forming an unwavering team, a melodious union that will guarantee collective excellence, a new commitment realised through promises and actions.Together, we produce champagnes that are the essence of finesse, lightness and elegance, champagnes that speak right to the heart of professionals and consumers alike.Champagnes that not only respect the terroir but exalt it. Champagnes that champion the French tradition of creativity whilst looking to the future with the next generation of passionate gourmets leading the world of gastronomy.
3_second_reach: Duval-Leroy — one of the last major independent, family-run Champagne houses, led by Carol Duval-Leroy. Femme is Grand Cru fruit only.

$title: Chateau des Jacques Clos de Rochegres Moulin-A-Vent 2020 750ml
$description: This is a Cru Beaujolais assembled from eight unique climats within the Moulin-a-Vent appellation. Each site presents it's own version of pink granite and exposure, which influences the eventual wine. All fruit is manually harvested, rigorously sorted, fermented with natural yeasts, and aged in concrete vats and oak barrels for 10 months. The final assemblage expresses the complete symphony of the Moulin-à-Vent appellation. HARVEST NOTE This was a very warm and early vintage with a slight lack of moisture which reduced the harvest volumes while ensuring complexity and phenolic ripeness TASTING NOTE This wine exudes dark fruit and floral aromas with hints of ground coffee. Bold and expansive on the palate, the flavor evolution is shaped by substantial yet fine tannins and tangy acidity over the long finish.
3_second_reach: Château des Jacques — Louis Jadot's flagship Beaujolais estate. Clos de Rochegrès is one of Moulin-à-Vent's most structured, age-worthy single vineyards.

$title: Pas de Probleme Pinot Noir France 750ml
$description: Pas de Problème wine originates from the Languedoc region's vineyards, nestled in the historic hill-town of Enserune, a mere 15 minutes southwest of Béziers. The soil in this area is reminiscent of the renowned terroirs of Burgundy, fostering ideal conditions for the vines to thrive, with a focus on achieving a harmonious balance and pronounced minerality. Situated 20 minutes from the Mediterranean Sea, the vineyard benefits from both maritime and continental climates. The warm days promote perfect ripeness, while the cool nights retain the grapes' inherent freshness. The vineyard practices sustainable farming, eschewing the use of chemicals, herbicides, and pesticides.To ensure a rich concentration of flavors, yields are restricted to under 45 hectoliters per hectare. During harvest, the grapes are handpicked and gently placed into small crates to maintain their integrity until they are crushed. The winemaking process involves meticulous destemming and inspection to prevent any stems from entering the extraction phase, which could impart undesirable green notes to the wine. The grapes undergo a cold maceration for eight days, with periodic punch-downs to enhance the aromatic profile. Fermentation then commences naturally and unfolds over a fortnight. To preserve the wine's fruity essence and freshness, it is aged for nine months in stainless steel tanks and is bottled without fining or filtration.
3_second_reach: Pas de Problème — 30-year-old Pinot Noir vines on Burgundy-like limestone outside Béziers. The 'no problem' answer when someone wants Pinot without the Burgundy bill.

$description: Winery: Founded 2016 by Avi Deixler in a barn on a working dairy farm in Point Reyes, Marin County — he's literally the only registered winery in the North Marin Wine District, a status he had to fight the Marin County Planning Commission to secure. Trained in California, Oregon, Australia, and France before starting his own thing, with a stated philosophy of using nothing but grapes: no additions, native yeast, hand-harvested, dry-farmed fruit. He's since expanding into a new facility in Mendocino County, sourcing largely from Poor Ranch in Hopland (organically farmed since the 1970s, sandy soils, old head-pruned vines 10–40 years old). The grape: Abouriou is a nearly extinct grape from Villeréal in Southwest France. Its name means "early" in Occitan, for its early ripening. Phylloxera wiped out nearly all of it in the 19th century; it survived only because a farmer discovered forgotten vines still growing up the wall of a ruined castle, and a private breeder named Numa Naugé propagated cuttings from them starting in 1882 — the grape's alternate name, Précoce Naugé, honors him. Today there's under 900 acres of it planted anywhere in the world. Very few American producers work with it at all. Winemaking: Manually harvested, whole clusters fermented in raw oak with barrel rolling (used here instead of punch-downs or pump-overs) for 10 days, pressed, then back into raw oak to age a full year. Unfined, unfiltered, no added sulfites. 14.5% ABV. Tasting notes: Fruity, lively, rustic — strawberry and vanilla aromatics, fruit-forward palate of red berries and cherries with a hint of spice, long tannins. Food pairings: Grilled sausage, roast pork, charcuterie boards, tomato-based pasta — rustic food for a rustic wine.
3_second_reach: Absentee Winery — Avi Deixler's barn on a Point Reyes dairy farm, Absentee — pouring Abouriou, a French grape that survived only because someone found it climbing the wall of a ruined castle.

$description: Syrah-dominant blend with Carignan, Petite Sirah, Abouriou The name: Balou is Avi Deixler's dog — his co-pilot on drives into San Francisco to sell the wine to sommeliers in the early days. It's become one of the winery's signature cuvées, named for the dog with, as one profile put it, a shared "rustic bouquet." Genuinely charming, low-key story, good for social copy. Winery: Same as Flaws — Avi Deixler, founded 2016, the only registered winery in Marin's North Marin Wine District, now expanding into Mendocino County. Same minimal-intervention philosophy: nothing but grapes, native yeast, no additions. Winemaking: Whole cluster, two-week maceration, fermented in raw French oak barrique that Deixler shaves down before every new fermentation, barrels sealed and rolled every few days (his signature technique instead of punch-downs), pressed, then back into the same barrel to age a year. No added SO2. Tasting notes: Robust fruit and spice, chewy tannins, fresh. Cherry and raspberry with peppery, savory notes — a big, rustic red built for grilling. Food pairings: Barbecue or steak, straight from the producer's own description — "the kind of big red you can enjoy anytime."
3_second_reach: Balou — named for Avi Deixler's dog, who rode shotgun on every trip into San Francisco to sell this wine one sommelier at a time.

$description: Clear bright ruby color with very light garnet red reflections; intense and persistent aroma of red fruit with notes of plum and cherry. A pleasant aroma of wood is noticeable after the fruity aroma, anticipating the full taste of a great wine suitable for long lasting life. A succulent, rich, full-bodied and pleasant taste emerges after the woody one, with the presence of slightly ripe red fruit. “Packaged with the black label, the Boroli 2019 Barolo Brunella draws its fruit from a choice vineyard site in Castiglione Falletto. This wine shows great balance between dark fruit, mineral and spice. It gives equal billing to all these important aromatic pieces to create nice harmony with long-lasting effects. Brunello also tends to show the most structure and fruit weight among these new releases.” - Wine Advocate Aug '23, 92pts
3_second_reach: Boroli — a family Barolo estate holding vineyards in Serralunga and Cerequio, two of the appellation's most prized crus.

$title: Penfolds Grange Shiraz Reserve Australia 2019 750ml +14% ABV
$description: The most powerful expression of Penfolds' multi-vineyard, multi-district blending philosophy, Grange is arguably Australia’s most celebrated wine and is officially listed as a Heritage Icon of South Australia. Crafted with fully-ripe, intensely-flavored and structured shiraz grapes, the result is a uniquely Australian style that is now recognized as one of the most consistent among the world’s great wines. Since its first experimental 1951 vintage, Grange has clearly demonstrated the synergy between shiraz and South Australia's soils and climates. Deep plush garnet throughout – from core to rim. Savoury, not fruity. Tastes/flavors remind of slow cooked beef ragout, chicken liver game terrine. Red liquorice also apparent. Integrated oak – spicy, almost ‘non-American’ oak … but it is. As it always is. A core of 100% new Quercus alba. Poised yet powerful. A balanced, tightly-knit and woven structural ‘tapestry’. Not to be constrained by dimension or frame.
3_second_reach: Penfolds Grange — Max Schubert's 1951 creation and still Australia's single most iconic wine. Multi-region Barossa Shiraz, built to outlive you.

$title: Stoller Family Estate Pinot Noir Willamette Valley 750ml
$description: This wine is composed of a purposeful selection of sites across the Willamette Valley AVA that best represent the spirit, quality, and ethos of what has made this part of Oregon so special. After a brief cold soak, these lots were fermented for between 10-12 days before gently pressing off the skins. A careful selection of oak totaling no more than 15% offered an elegant framing for such a late vintage.
3_second_reach: Stoller — Bill Stoller's Dundee Hills estate, home to the first LEED Gold-certified winery in the country. Sustainable, top to bottom.

$description: Soft, light, and approachable Nebbiolo more so, than usually found in young wine of this type. Aldo and Milena Vajra are among the quietest and most introspective of Piedmont’s top echelon growers. It is the wines that do the talking here, and they do that ever so eloquently. Vajra's Langhe Nebbiolo (from the estate’s youngest vines) is another impeccable, harmonious wine laced with plump, perfumed Nebbiolo fruit. The Langhe Nebbiolo offers outstanding length in a soft, accessible style that is sure to find many admirers. This is a great bottle of wine for the money!
3_second_reach: G.D. Vajra — the Vaira family's organic Barolo estate in Vergne. This Langhe Nebbiolo is the same grape, the everyday version.

$description: Styled in the mold of classic Beaujolais Nouveau, this light red is very fresh with light and crunchy tannins. Bright acid helps accentuate its mouthwatering fruit profile with just a hint of carbonic character to tie it all together. Perfect to enjoy with friends around your holiday tables. At Les Lunes Wine we lease our own vineyards, work our own vines and built our own cellar. We're blazing our own trail like the pioneering winemakers of California. Our goal is to grow wines that pay respect to the great wines of California’s past. We do very little in the cellar because we spend time in our vineyards. Proper pruning, precise suckering, well-timed treatments and thoughtful weed management lets us minimize the pesticide inputs in our vineyards. We do this to preserve the indigenous microbes on the grapes and in the soils, which leads to healthier and more complex wines that don’t need adjusting or stabilizing. Our goal year in and year out is to bring you a unique taste of the distinct times and places which we love and tend. The care that we bring through the entire winegrowing process shines through into the final product. Our wines are balanced in their youth, but the care we invest in the winegrowing will continue to reverberate in your cellar for years to come.
3_second_reach: Les Lunes — a natural-wine project spanning Napa, Sonoma, and Mendocino. This Nouveau is Beaujolais-style, carbonic, and meant to be drunk now.

$title: la Pepee Pinot Noir Arbois 2022 750 ml
$description: La Pepée is his first Pinot Noir, sourced from two vineyards, one near La Mulatiere and the other near Les Bodines. The vines are planted in clay soils and are vinified using the same techniques as Tôt ou Tard. Élevage is a bit different, with half of the juice pressed into 600L barriques and the rest into stainless steel. He then adds a bit of SO2 at bottling, depending on the vintage.
3_second_reach: La Pépée — Jean-Baptiste Menigoz's Jura natural-wine project. Whole-cluster Pinot Noir, floral, lavender-scented, nothing like Burgundy.

$description: 100% Niellucciu, a native Corsican grape variety closely related to Sangiovese, known for producing structured, aromatic red wines. Inky black with crimson edges. Complex bouquet of black plum, eucalyptus, dried green herbs, violet petals, and hints of black truffle and dark coffee. Medium-plus bodied, dry, with notes of black cherry, stewed red fruits, purple flowers, and an earthy backbone. It features firm, powdery tannins and surprising acidity, balancing the rich fruit.
3_second_reach: Clos Marfisi — fifth-generation siblings farming Corsica's Patrimonio appellation organically, a kilometer from the sea.

$description: Winery: Marie Thibault isn't from a winemaking family — she has degrees in biology and oenology, cut her teeth working under François Chidaine (one of the Loire's most respected Chenin Blanc producers) in Montlouis, then founded her own 3.5-hectare domaine in Azay-le-Rideau in 2011, a lesser-known corner of Touraine. Small operation: 4,000–5,000 cases a year across her whole range (Gamay, Côt, Grolleau, Chenin Blanc). This specific wine: 'Les Grandes Vignes' is named for one specific parcel — old vines averaging 50 years, on the southern slope of the Indre river, flint (silex) soil over clay-limestone bedrock. Native/spontaneous fermentation after crushing, 10 months macerating on the skins with décuvage (drawing off) in July, then bottled without fining, filtration, or added sulfites — a genuine natural wine, not just marketed as one. 100% Gamay, Touraine/Azay-le-Rideau, Loire Valley Tasting notes: Very textured and deep, with a notable smokiness over earthy red-berry fruit. The importer's own copy calls her wines "bold and strong," suggesting a year or two in bottle to really show well. Food pairings: Casual, rustic fare — barbecue, roast chicken, charcuterie, mushroom dishes. Think cru Beaujolais pairing territory given the smoky, earthy Gamay character.
3_second_reach: Marie Thibault — trained under Loire legend François Chidaine on Chenin Blanc, but 'Les Grandes Vignes' is her ode to Gamay: one 50-year-old vine parcel on pure flint, zero additions.

$title: Domaine de L'Harmas Chateauneuf du Pape 750ml 2022 +14% ABV
$description: Domaine de L'Harmas was created in 2000 by Patrick and Nathalie Fabre. However the vineyards were in the family for 4th generation and the grapes sold to the local coop. The estate is certified Organic since 2012. The 3.5 ha of Chateauneuf du Pape are adjacent to Chateau de Beaucastel. This cuvee presents notes of black fruit, spices such as clove, nutmeg and pepper. Full-bodied and powerful mouth.
3_second_reach: Domaine de l'Harmas — certified-organic vines that sit right next door to Château de Beaucastel. Same neighborhood, friendlier price.

$description: The Pierre-Henri Rougeot Corton Grand Cru 2022 is a red wine from the Burgundy region of France, specifically the Côte de Beaune, made from 100% Pinot Noir. Produced by Pierre-Henri Rougeot, a young vigneron from Meursault, this wine comes from his small-scale négociant operation, emphasizing organic farming and minimal intervention. The wine is crafted with 100% whole-bunch vinification, resulting in a deep, rich purple color with a slight vegetal note, dark raspberry, and bramble flavors. It offers a balanced profile with fine tannins, good length, and a stemmy style that flows across the palate without heat. The production is limited, reflecting Rougeot’s low-intervention approach: no SO2 until bottling, no fining, no filtration, and aging in neutral barrels.
3_second_reach: Pierre-Henri Rougeot — the same young Côte de Nuits grower, here at the very top: a tiny-production Corton Grand Cru.

$description: Pertois-Moriset made this wine to celebrate their return to the Club Trésors de Champagne, a prestigious group of artisan winemakers. It shows fresh mineral and chalk aromas—as well as a creamy, delicate palate and toasty structure—from Chardonnay grown on the house’s best sites in the Grand Cru village of Mesnil-sur-Oger. On the nose this has a mineral, creamy chalk, fresh aroma. The palate has an aromatic, creamy, delicate, mineral, nutty, rich/intense, toasty structure.
3_second_reach: Pertois-Moriset — same Le Mesnil-sur-Oger family, same prestigious Special Club cuvée, now in a magnum built for a table that wants a show.

$description: Features a profusion of dark fruits (blackberry, cassis) with floral notes, hints of licorice, and peonies. Sturdy and structured with robust fruitiness dominating in its youth. It offers an ample core of fruit, soft tannins, and mild acidity, with a clean, fresh energy that carries through to the palate. The wine is described as elegant rather than a blockbuster, with youthfully chewy tannins.
3_second_reach: Louis Jadot — one of Burgundy's great négociant houses, here at the Côte de Nuits' most affordable address, Marsannay.

$title: Pierre-Henri Rougeot Cotes de Nuits Villages Les Plantes du Bois 2022 750ml
$description: The wine has an intense, dark robe for a Pinot Noir. On the nose, it offers prominent notes of small stone fruits like sour cherry, with the pit more pronounced than the fruit itself, accompanied by perceptible acidity, smokiness, and noble spice. In the mouth, the tannins are present but not fully integrated, suggesting potential for further aging. The 2022 Pierre-Henri Rougeot Côte de Nuits Villages 'Les Plantes du Bois' is a red wine made from Pinot Noir, produced in the Burgundy region of France, specifically from the village of Comblanchien on a mid-slope, clay-limestone terroir. This cuvée, named "the plants of the forest," is crafted by Pierre-Henri Rougeot, a respected winemaker known for his minimal-intervention approach and organic farming practices.
3_second_reach: Pierre-Henri Rougeot — a Meursault-trained grower working tiny parcels across the Côte de Nuits. This is the accessible door into a portfolio that gets very hard to find.

$description: A name that means “donna in fuga” (woman in flight) and refers to the story of a queen who found refuge in the part of Sicily where the company’s vineyards are located today. Donnafugata, founded in 1983, is guided by the fifth generation of the experienced winemaking Rallo family. This highly rated fresh and cheerful white wine from Sicily is medium-bodied with crisp acidity. Aromas and flavors are all over the board with stone fruits, tropical fruits, honeydew, Meyer lemon, Mediterranean herbs, and tree fruits all making an appearance.
3_second_reach: Donnafugata — the Rallo family estate that put modern Sicilian wine on the map. SurSur is their Grillo, straight off the island's west coast.

$title: Belle Glos Clark & Telephone Pinot Noir Santa Maria Valley 750ml +14% ABV
$description: The Clark & Telephone Vineyard was established in 1972 and planted with “own root” Martini clone vines. Located just 13 miles from the ocean and situated on a west-facing slope, this vineyard experiences weather patterns that pull from west to east to bring cool fog and coastal breezes inland until August when Santa Ana winds begin. We harvested early in the morning so the fruit would arrive at the winery while the grapes were still cool to preserve their vineyard-fresh flavors. After destemming (but not crushing) the berries, we cold-soaked the must for 14 days to soften the skins and allow for ideal extraction. During fermentation in a combination of closed and open-top stainless steel fermenters, we used both punch-down and pump-over techniques to extract color and phenolics. We aged the wine in 100% French oak (60% new) for up to 12 months. After the wine underwent malolactic fermentation, we racked it twice before bottling. Tasting Notes Deep ruby red in color with lush aromas of ripe cherry, nutmeg, dark chocolate and holiday baking spices. Bold and complex flavors of black plum, crushed raspberry and blueberry pie linger on the palate. The texture is rich and lively, and leads into a warm and structured finish.
3_second_reach: Belle Glos — Joseph Wagner's (yes, that Caymus family) single-vineyard Pinot Noir project. Clark & Telephone is the bold, dark-fruited one.

$title: Le Mistral Syrah Brosseau Vineyard Chalone 750ml
$description: We started using less new French oak in this and letting the peppery and juicy grapes speak to you directly. This wine has a wonderfully savory and briny nature that is intriguing in its youth but will age very nicely over the next 5-25 years. The Syrah was hand-harvested along with the Viognier and co-fermented in open-top bins. We always place the whole cluster portion in the bin first, then the de-stemmed fruit on top afterward. The wine is natively fermented before aging in French oak (25% one year old) for 16 months before bottling in the winter of 2022.
3_second_reach: Le Mistral — reaching into the Chalone AVA's Brosseau Vineyard for cool-climate Syrah with genuine Rhône backbone.

$description: Plum, Black Currant, Vanilla, Tobacco Our winemaker possesses a deep passion for Merlot, a grape variety that compliments Bordeaux grapes in Texas. By combining grapes from two vineyards in the High Plains, both owned by childhood friends, we aim to capture the essence of their enduring friendship through our wine blend. This creation is an authentic portrayal of Texas Merlot.
3_second_reach: Hilmy Cellars — 100% Texas fruit, and this Merlot just out-poured the whole state: Reserve Grand Champion at Houston's Rodeo Uncorked.

$description: A clean yet classic expression of the Roussanne grape, with all of the fruitiness that we’d expect, but with a surprisingly high-toned nature. This wine is mineral, lean, very dry, and tense. Perfect for the lover of many French white wines.
3_second_reach: Bingham Family Vineyards — 250 estate acres on the Texas High Plains built around Rhône whites, and Roussanne is where they shine brightest.

$title: Pebble Rock Cellars Teroldego Texas High Plains 2020 750ml
$description: Fruit: Bright red berries like cranberry, pomegranate, and raspberry, with hints of blackberry. Spice & Earth: Peppery spice, subtle cinnamon or anise, and black earth/mineral undertones. Structure: Fresh acidity balances the fruit, with soft, dusty tannins from oak aging—making it versatile for early drinking (now through 2028) without needing further cellaring.
3_second_reach: Pebble Rock Cellars — a Johnson City husband-and-wife team pouring a grape almost no one else in Texas dares to plant: Teroldego.

$title: Hye Meadow Winery Chenin Blanc 'Cerro Santo Vineyard' Texas High Plains 2023 750ml
$description: A "beautifully balanced" wine: Aroma: Subtle oak and honeycomb notes. Palate: High acidity with a long finish; flavors of grapefruit, baking spices, and returning oak influence. Aging: 10 months in new French oak, adding structure without overpowering the fruit.
3_second_reach: Hye Meadow — a Highway 290 fixture since before Hill Country wine was cool, pouring Chenin Blanc off their own High Plains vineyard, Cerro Santo.

$title: Rochioli Pinot Noir Russian River Valley 2023 750ml +14%
$description: Elegant and beautifully balanced, this Pinot Noir has aromas of ripe cherry, vanilla and a hint of savory herbs, while on the palate it is juicy and refined with a hint of dusty cherry. The wine has a big rich mouth-feel, silky tannins and a long finish. This wine expresses classic Rochioli character.
3_second_reach: Rochioli — the family that's farmed Russian River's most coveted Pinot vineyards since the 1930s. The name that basically built the appellation.

$title: Two Squared Cabernet Sauvignon Napa Valley 2022 750ml +14%
$description: Winery: Two Squared is the "second label" of Alpha Omega Winery, a well-regarded Rutherford Bench producer in Napa. Launched in 2009, it follows the classic Bordeaux model — top châteaux have long made a more approachable "second wine" from younger vines alongside their flagship — sourced from small, lesser-known "hidden gem" Napa vineyards, made to drink well immediately rather than age for a decade. It now sits under the "Alpha Omega Collective" umbrella alongside Tolosa (Central Coast), with production centered in San Luis Obispo. For 2022 specifically, a significant portion of the fruit came from the Oak Knoll AVA. Tasting notes: Deep to opaque ruby red. Nose of ripe plum, dark cherry, and boysenberry with worcestershire and cedar notes. Palate is medium-full bodied — cassis, red currant, dark earth, dried tobacco, toast, firm structured finish. Fermented in stainless, aged 9 months in French oak (20% new). 15% ABV. (75% Cabernet Sauvignon, 16% Petit Verdot, 9% Malbec) Critic score: 93 points, Wine Enthusiast (Elaine Chukan Brown) — "generous, full-bodied and bold... plush... fine, firm tannins carry through a persistent finish." The brand also has some pedigree behind it: Wine Spectator's James Molesworth featured the Two Squared Red 2021 in "8 Amazing West Coast Cabernets at $50 or Less." Food pairings: Given the structure and tannin — grilled steak, braised short rib, lamb chops, aged cheddar or gouda.
3_second_reach: Two Squared — Alpha Omega's more approachable Napa Cabernet, made by the same Jean Hoefliger and Michel Rolland pairing, built to drink the day you open it.

$description: With its pale yellow robe, Château Pilet Blanc is a fruity and generous wine, displaying nice notes of citrus and exotic fruit on the nose and on the palate.
3_second_reach: Château Pilet — an Entre-Deux-Mers family estate proving Bordeaux Blanc doesn't have to be expensive to be citrusy and precise.

$title: Jean-Luc Colombo Les Abeilles Cotes du Rhone Rouge 750ml
$description: Intense purple color, seductive aromas of red fruits, coriander and bay leaf. This is a fresh and silky wine, with notes of licorice and spice on the palate.
3_second_reach: Jean-Luc Colombo — the Cornas winemaker who helped put Northern Rhône Syrah on the map, naming his everyday cuvée after the bees in his own vines.

$title: DeLoach Vineyards OFS Zinfandel Russian River Valley 2016 750ml +14%
$description: Our Finest Selection - Rich & Intense
3_second_reach: DeLoach — Biodynamic-certified Russian River estate, and OFS is their old-vine Zinfandel flagship. 'Our Founder's Selection' means they mean it.

$description: Aromas on the nose of the 2023 Napa Valley Chardonnay reveal lively notes of white pineapple, lemon curd, and apricot preserves, with hints of jasmine and orange blossom followed by a touch of ocean salinity. The palate is complex with flavors of white peach, lemon meringue, toasted vanilla bean, wet stone, and crushed granite that join with a vibrant, balanced acidity making this Chardonnay extremely versatile for pairing with a variety of dishes. This medium-bodied Chardonnay is creamy, round, bright and balanced, delighting the senses.
3_second_reach: Sequoia Grove — Rutherford, Napa, since 1978. Old-guard family winery, new-vintage Chardonnay, same steady hand.

$description: True to our heritage of producing top-tier Cabernet Sauvignon, this wine showcases a seamless blend of elegance and strength. It begins with captivating aromas of dark red berries and cardamom, leading the way to a defined palate that showcases flavors of fig jam and boysenberry pie. Firm, dusty tannins provide a sturdy foundation, guiding you to a long, focused finish that denotes a harmonious blend of mountain and valley floor fruit.
3_second_reach: Duckhorn — Napa's founding Merlot specialist since 1976. Same polished house style, now poured into Cabernet.

$title: Piper-Heidsieck Rare Brut Rose Millesime Champagne 750ml
$description: The wine is celebrated for its power, elegance, and complexity. Nose — Exuberant red and dark fruits (wild strawberry, blackberry, black cherry, raspberry), blood orange, citrus (grapefruit), floral notes (rose petals, peony), and hints of spice or exotic herbs. Palate — Velvety and generous, with flavors of strawberry tart, crème pâtissière, chocolate, pink peppercorn, kirsch, and a vinous tension. Fine mousse, bright acidity, and a long, saline or bitter finish. Overall — Balances energy and finesse; powerful yet refined, often praised for evolving beautifully in the glass. Critics frequently score it highly (95–98+ points from Wine Advocate, Jeb Dunnuck, Falstaff, etc.), noting its structure and aging potential (drink now through 2035–2045 for recent vintages).
3_second_reach: Piper-Heidsieck — a Reims house dating to 1785. Rare is their prestige tier, made only when the vintage earns it.

$title: EnRoute Pinot Noir Les Pommiers Russian River Valley 2023 750ml +14%
$description: Blended from three of the most coveted vineyards in the Russian River Valley, the 2023 vintage opens with aromas of Bing Cherry that are complemented by notes of muddled blackberry, baking spice, Oolong tea, and candied orange peel. Generous yet soft dark berry flavors expand on the palate, with elegant, silky tannins. A truly incredible Pinot Noir that should be in any collector's repertoire.
3_second_reach: EnRoute — Far Niente's dedicated Pinot Noir project, from the same family that's run one of Napa's most storied estates since 1885.

$title: Burgess Red Blend Alpinist Napa Valley 2015 750ml +14%
$description: The 2015 Alpinist is a red blend from historic Burgess Cellars in Napa Valley, California. This wine marked the inaugural vintage under the "Alpinist" name (previously called "Mountaineer" in 2013–2014). It's an unconventional Napa blend, primarily ~50% Cabernet Sauvignon and ~50% Syrah, with smaller additions of Petite Sirah and Petit Verdot. Sourced from hillside vineyards, including influences from the estate's slopes on Howell Mountain. Tasting Notes and Style Reviewers describe it as: Medium- to full-bodied Juicy and balanced, with vibrant red and black fruit flavors (blueberries, tart cherries, blackberries, plums) Hints of spice, cocoa, and subtle oak Fresh acidity, silky tannins, and a mouthwatering finish It's often praised as a refreshing alternative to the bigger, more opulent Napa Cabernets—elegant and food-friendly rather than overpowering. Burgess Cellars has a rich history dating back to the late 19th century, when Swiss-Italian immigrants first planted vines on Howell Mountain. Tom Burgess founded the modern winery in 1972 on the site of the original Souverain Cellars (where legends like Mike Grgich and Warren Winiarski got their start). The winery was family-owned until 2020, when it was acquired by the Lawrence family (owners of Heitz Cellars); tragically, the original hillside facility was destroyed shortly after in the 2020 Glass Fire, but production continues with a focus on regenerative farming.
3_second_reach: Burgess — Howell Mountain fruit since 1972, before anyone wanted mountain wine. Now that structure is exactly what collectors chase.

$title: Domaine Serene "Willamette Pinot Noir Barrel Auction" 2014 Evenstad Estate Pinor Noir Dundee Hills  750ml +14%
$description: This is a single-barrel selection from Domaine Serene's flagship Evenstad Estate Vineyard in the Dundee Hills AVA, Willamette Valley, Oregon. The 2014 vintage was part of the inaugural Willamette: The Pinot Noir Auction (originally called the Willamette: The Pinot Noir Barrel Auction), a trade-only event held in April 2016 by the Willamette Valley Wineries Association. Auction details: Auction #1 (the first edition), Lot #53. Producers like Domaine Serene donated unique lots—often 5-10 cases (60-120 bottles) from a single standout barrel or special selection of the prior vintage (here, 2014, an excellent, balanced year in Oregon). These bottles are hand-numbered #35 of 72, with a special neck label referencing "the pinot noir barrel auction" and signed.
3_second_reach: Domaine Serene — Ken and Grace Evenstad's Dundee Hills icon, and this is the bottling from their own home vineyard.

$description: Benoît Courault "Gilbourg" 2023 is a highly regarded natural white wine from the Loire Valley, France. Producer: Benoît Courault, a respected natural winemaker based in Faye d'Anjou (Anjou region). He transitioned from sommelier to vigneron, training in Beaune and working with icons like Dominique Derain, Yvon Métras, and especially Eric Pfifferling (Domaine l'Anglore). He farms about 5 hectares of old vines organically, using draft horses for plowing, herbal treatments, and minimal intervention. Grape & Style: 100% Chenin Blanc from vines around 40+ years old on schistous/clay-schist soils. It's often described as his "tête de cuvée" (top white), pure, vibrant, and elegant—considered one of the best natural Chenins from the Loire. Winemaking: Hand-harvested, long gentle press, spontaneous fermentation with native yeasts in used barrels or foudres, aged 8–12 months in oak. No fining, no filtration, and little to no added SO₂ (often none or tiny amounts). Natural wine approach. Tasting Notes: Expect complex fruit (pear, yellow fruits, apple, peach, acacia flowers), minerality, freshness, balance between amplitude and tension, with a long, saline finish. Pure, intense, and harmonious—drinkable now but with aging potential.
3_second_reach: Benoit Courault — an Anjou natural winemaker working old vines with almost no added sulfur. Gilbourg is one single parcel, bottled alone.

$description: Benoît Courault "Empreinte" 2023 is a natural white wine from the Loire Valley, France, produced by the same acclaimed winemaker as Gilbourg. Producer: Benoît Courault, based in Faye-d’Anjou (Anjou region). His philosophy remains organic farming with draft horses, minimal intervention, and a focus on purity and terroir expression, influenced by his time at Domaine l'Anglore. Grape & Style: 100% Chenin Blanc. This is a relatively newer cuvée in his lineup (around its third or fourth vintage by 2023), often described as fine, delicate, gourmand yet refined—more accessible and approachable than his flagship Gilbourg, with a balance of fruitiness and minerality. Winemaking: Hand-harvested grapes, direct gentle pressing, spontaneous fermentation in used barrels (225L and 600L), aged on lees for about 6–12 months. No fining, no filtration, and typically no or very minimal added SO₂ (often none). Tasting Notes: Ripe yellow fruits (pear, peach), hints of almond and subtle smokiness, fresh acidity, mineral tension, and a long, elegant finish. It's generous and expressive but precise—simple yet sophisticated, highly drinkable young but with potential to evolve. Comparison to Gilbourg: While Gilbourg is often his "tête de cuvée" (top Chenin from older vines, more intense and structured), Empreinte is seen as a more immediate, fruit-forward expression, sometimes from slightly different or younger parcels, making it a great entry point to his whites.
3_second_reach: While Gilbourg is often his "tête de cuvée" (top Chenin from older vines, more intense and structured), Empreinte is seen as a more immediate, fruit-forward expression, sometimes from slightly different or younger parcels, making it a great entry point to his whites.

$title: Rijckaert Arbois Grand Elevage Savagnin Jura 2022 750ml
$description: Rijckaert Arbois Grand Elevage Savagnin 2022 is a white wine from the Arbois appellation in France's Jura region, produced by Domaine Rijckaert (now under winemaker Florent Rouve, who took over from founder Jean Rijckaert). It's made from 100% Savagnin grapes, often from old vines (vieilles vignes), and is an ouillé (topped-up) style—unlike oxidative Vin Jaune, it's aged to preserve freshness while gaining complexity. Key Details Winemaking: Aged around 24 months on lees in barrels, with occasional bâtonnage (stirring) and topping up to avoid oxidation. This results in a rich, structured wine with minerality and salinity. Tasting Notes: Expect aromas of ripe yellow apple, lemon/citrus zest, bergamot, and subtle cedar or nutty hints (almonds, hazelnuts). On the palate, it's powerful and dense, with chewiness, fruity/sappy notes, intense minerality, and an impressive saline, long finish. It's full-bodied yet fresh, with great purity and complexity. Pairings: Excellent with Comté cheese, pork dishes, potatoes, rich poultry, or mountain cheeses—its salinity and acidity cut through richness beautifully. Style Note: This is a non-oxidative Savagnin (non-ouillé would be more nutty/sherry-like), showcasing the grape's potential for elegance and depth.
3_second_reach: Rijckaert — Jean Rijckaert, co-founder of Verget, left Burgundy to champion the Jura's Savagnin. Now his protégé Florent Rouve carries it forward.

$title: Domaine Valentin Zussliin Pinot Auxerrois Au'rigine Alsace 2022 750ml
$description: Domaine Valentin Zusslin "Au'rigine" Pinot Auxerrois 2022 is a biodynamic dry white wine from Alsace, France. This historic estate, founded in 1691 in Orschwihr (southern Alsace), is run by siblings Marie and Jean-Paul Zusslin. They have practiced biodynamic farming (Demeter-certified) since 1997 across their key terroirs: Bollenberg, Clos Liebenberg (monopole), and Grand Cru Pfingstberg. Key Details Grape: 100% Pinot Auxerrois (a traditional Alsace variety, often blended but rare as a varietal still wine). Winemaking: Whole-cluster direct pressing → native yeast fermentation in large old oak tuns (foudres) with no additives → aged 12–18 months on fine lees for texture and balance → bottled with minimal sulfur. Style: Elegant, fresh, and aromatic with fruity notes (pear, apple, citrus), supple mouthfeel, and lively acidity. Low alcohol (around 11.5–12%) makes it highly digestible and food-friendly. Critical Acclaim: La Revue du vin de France praises it as "magnifiquement digeste, aérien et suave" (beautifully digestible, airy, and suave). This cuvée pays homage to "origin" (a play on "Au'rigine"), highlighting Auxerrois' historical role at the domaine.
3_second_reach: Domaine Valentin Zusslin — Demeter-certified biodynamic in Alsace for generations, still bothering with Pinot Auxerrois, a grape most producers ignore.

$description: Hervé Villemade "Désiré" Cheverny Rouge 2020 (1.5L magnum) is a rare, special cuvée from Domaine Hervé Villemade in the Cheverny appellation of the Loire Valley, France. This wine comes from very old-vine Pinot Noir planted by the producer's grandfather (Désiré, hence the name). It's produced only in exceptional vintages and bottled exclusively in magnum format (1.5L). Key Details: Grape: 100% Pinot Noir (unlike the estate's standard Cheverny Rouge, which blends ~60% Pinot Noir with 40% Gamay). Style: Natural, minimalist winemaking — organic farming, native yeasts, whole-cluster fermentation (often 15-20 days), aging in vessels like qvevri, barrels, or amphorae, with little to no added sulfur. Expect elegant, fresh, pure Pinot character: red berries (raspberry, cherry), finesse, soft tannins, minerality, and earthy notes. Producer: Hervé Villemade, a pioneer in natural wines in Cheverny (Cellettes), farming ~22-25 hectares organically since 2000. Imported in the US by Louis/Dressner Selections. Rarity: Magnum-only and vintage-dependent, so limited availability.
3_second_reach: Hervé Villemade — a Loire natural-wine legend who went organic in 2000, taking his cues straight from Marcel Lapierre.

$description: The 2020 Bodyguard is the newest edition to this exceptional collection from winemaker Daniel Daou. Bold and brooding, it displays a vivid, deep purple hue accompanied by an intense nose of chocolate-covered blueberry, black raspberry, Zante currant, pencil lead and damp forest floor. Secondary layers reveal notes of kirsch, fennel, black olive and a hint of cool wintergreen. A lush palate of black plum, dried cherry and blackberry is supported by a firm structure with polished fine-grained tannins. Highlights of dusty leather, dried sage and truffle add layers of complexity that complement the rich, dark fruit. The finish strikes an impressive balance of power and grace, with lingering notes of currant, dark chocolate and crushed stone minerality that enhance the fullness of the experience. 91-93 Points, Jeb Dunnuck
3_second_reach: DAOU — the Adelaida District estate that turned Paso Robles into cult-Cabernet country in under a decade.

$description: "The Bourgogne Chardonnay is a still, dry, white wine with fruit aromas (lychee, pear). As a result of the perfect location, the sugar content can reach a high level whilst maintaining a balance of fruit and acidity. It is rapidly available for a tasting. Produced in the commune of Puligny-Montrachet, our Chardonnay is a very fine representative of the grape, noble and straight."
3_second_reach: Domaine Jomain — a Chassagne-Montrachet family estate, so even their entry-level Bourgogne Blanc carries real white-Burgundy pedigree.

$title: PerUs 'Bryn' Proprietary Red Blend Napa Valley 2021 750ml +14%
$description: The PerUs 'Bryn' Proprietary Red Blend Napa Valley 2021 is a limited-production, high-end red wine from PerUs Wine, a boutique Napa Valley producer founded by Anmol Bhandari. The winery focuses on ultra-premium, small-lot bottlings (often under allocation to members), with winemaking led by renowned consultant Russell Bevan (known for his work on powerful, expressive Napa reds). Key Details for the 2021 Vintage Blend Composition: 50% Cabernet Sauvignon from Tench Vineyard (Oakville area) + 50% Merlot from Sugarloaf Mountain Vineyard (hillside site southeast of Napa city). Production: Only about 100 cases made — very limited and collectible. Style and Tasting Notes: This is an elegant yet powerful Bordeaux-style blend. It features gorgeous blackberry and dark fruit aromas (blackberry, plum, blueberry), with notes of mocha, roasted coffee, spice, earth, and subtle chocolatey Merlot influences. On the palate, it's full-bodied with velvety texture, harmonious dark fruits, well-integrated tannins, and a smooth, lingering finish. The 2021 vintage brings concentration and power balanced by elegance — more polished and creamy than some edgier Napa vintages. Critic Scores / Reception: Community and early reviews highlight high quality (e.g., CellarTracker averages around 95.5 points from limited reviews; broader PerUs lineup often earns 94–98+ from critics like Jeb Dunnuck or James Suckling for similar vintages). It's described as rich, plush, and approachable yet age-worthy. Average Price: Around $199–$230 per 750ml bottle (ex-tax, based on secondary market data; retail/allocation pricing may vary). PerUs wines emphasize no-compromise quality from top sites, and 'Bryn' (named after a family member) often leans plush and fruit-forward compared to their more Cabernet-dominant labels.
3_second_reach: PerUs — Russell Bevan's other Napa blend, plusher than Pont, off the same Tench and Sugarloaf Mountain fruit.

$title: PerUs 'Pont' Proprietary Red Blend Napa Valley 2020 750ml +14%
$description: The PerUs 'Pont' Proprietary Red Blend Napa Valley 2020 is another limited-production Bordeaux-style red from the same boutique Napa producer (PerUs Wine, founded by Anmol Bhandari, with winemaking by consultant Russell Bevan). It's positioned as a more approachable and value-oriented entry in their lineup compared to some of their higher-end, Cabernet-dominant single-varietal or flagship blends. Key Details for the 2020 Vintage Blend Composition: 40% Cabernet Sauvignon (from Tench Vineyard in Oakville, a prestigious site neighboring icons like Screaming Eagle) + 35% Merlot + 25% Cabernet Franc (both from Sugarloaf Mountain Vineyard, a hillside site southeast of Napa with cooler influences). Production: Only about 300 cases made — still very limited, but larger than ultra-rare bottlings like some of their others (e.g., 'Bryn' at ~100 cases). Style and Tasting Notes (from producer and retailer descriptions): This vintage shows "amazing linear power" with a structured, energetic profile that's complex yet food-friendly. Aromas and flavors include tobacco, bright cherry, bittersweet chocolate, ripe red and blue fruits, cassis, dark chocolate, sweet tobacco, leather, and subtle spice. It's full-bodied with ripe yet poised fruit, supple tannins, good freshness, and a long, smooth finish. The 2020 Napa vintage was challenging (wildfires affected some areas), but this wine is noted for its balance, approachability in youth, and energy — more linear and focused than plush powerhouses, making it ideal for hearty, slow-cooked meals. Critic Scores / Reception: Limited professional reviews (no major scores from Parker/WA or Spectator noted), but community feedback on CellarTracker averages around 87–95 points from a small number of notes (e.g., one at 95 for complexity and red berries after opening; others note tannic structure and black cherry). Vivino users describe it as a solid, full-bodied everyday Napa red with dark fruit, leather, and tobacco. It's praised for punching above its weight in quality-to-price ratio. Compared to the 2021 'Bryn' (50/50 Cab Sauv/Merlot, more plush/velvety with darker fruits and higher scores/pricing ~$200+), 'Pont' leans toward brighter cherry/red fruit lift from the Cabernet Franc, with a more structured, food-driven personality — great for pairing with slow-roasted meats, Bolognese, game, or grilled lamb. It's often highlighted as a "gentleman's wine" in the lineup: refined, energetic, and enjoyable now with decanting, while still age-worthy for 10+ years.
3_second_reach: PerUs — Russell Bevan's Napa project, and this Cabernet comes off the Tench Vineyard. Its neighbor happens to be Screaming Eagle.

$description: The Pertois-Moriset Special Club Champagne 2016 is a prestigious Blanc de Blancs (100% Chardonnay) from the renowned Grand Cru village of Le Mesnil-sur-Oger in the Côte des Blancs region of Champagne, France. Produced by the family-owned estate Champagne Pertois-Moriset (founded in 1951), this cuvée celebrates their return to the elite Club Trésors de Champagne—a selective group of artisan grower-producers limited to around 28 members. Only exceptional vintages qualify for the "Special Club" designation after rigorous blind tastings by a professional jury. This 2016 vintage comes from top vineyard sites (some vines dating back to 1935), farmed sustainably or biodynamically, with hand-harvesting, fermentation primarily in stainless steel (with some oak), blocked malolactic fermentation for freshness, and extended lees aging (around 4 years) before disgorgement. The result is a dry, mineral-driven Champagne with low dosage (around 1.5g/L in similar profiles), emphasizing the chalky terroir of Le Mesnil-sur-Oger. Key Characteristics and Tasting Notes Appearance: Pale gold with fine, persistent bubbles. Nose: Fresh mineral and chalky aromas, creamy chalk, green apple, pear skin, light toast, crushed chalk, with notes of bread, biscuit, peach, and apple in more evolved tastings. Palate: Creamy and delicate mousse, aromatic with vibrant minerality, nutty and toasty elements, rich yet intense structure, high acidity, salinity, and a long, clean, tense finish. It balances maturity (yellow fruits, grapefruit, almond) with steely focus and finesse—often described as world-class, chiseled, and generous without heaviness. Style: Complex, traditional, earthy, and minerally; excellent aging potential.
3_second_reach: Pertois-Moriset — a Le Mesnil-sur-Oger grower family, and Special Club is one of the rarest honors in Champagne: fewer than 30 houses are even allowed to bottle it.

$title: Loewen Riesling Trocken 'Detzem Maximin Klosterlay' Mosel 2020 750ml
$description: Weingut Carl Loewen is a family-run estate in Leiwen (near Detzem/Trittenheim area) on the Mosel, with roots dating back to 1803 when they acquired parcels from the historic Benedictine Abbey of St. Maximin in Trier. The Maximin Klosterlay vineyard is one of their flagship sites—among the oldest and most significant in the Mosel, featuring blue slate soils that impart intense minerality. It's classified as an Erste Lage (premier cru equivalent). The 2020 vintage was produced as a dry Riesling (around 12.5% ABV), though the label sometimes omits "Trocken" for flexibility if residual sugar edges slightly over strict German thresholds—it's effectively dry with racy acidity. Tasting Notes and Reviews This wine is highly regarded for its elegance, precision, and terroir expression in a warm vintage like 2020, which brought sleek polish to many Mosel Rieslings. Aromas often include citrus (lemon, lime, grapefruit), stone fruit, wildflowers/herbs, and prominent slate/mineral notes. On the palate: Bright, medium-bodied, with zesty acidity, pliant texture, stony minerality, and a long, smoky/earthy finish. Some describe it as soulful yet precise, with "sponti" (spontaneous fermentation) character adding depth. Critic highlights (from sources like importer notes and reviews): Terry Theise (noted Mosel expert) praised the 2020 Maximin Klosterlay for its "perfectly wonderful" nose, sponti soulfulness, pliant texture against slatey chew, and an ancient smoke-like finish rising from underground fissures. He called the Loewen 2020s "heart-rending" in their delicate paradoxes—clear yet soft-lit, gentle yet forceful. Vivino and community notes frequently mention earthy/mineral tones, peach, ripe apple, lemon, apricot, with vivid acidity and great mouthfeel. Similar vintages (e.g., 2022) score highly (e.g., Wine Enthusiast praises fresh, pure zesty flavors of Meyer lemon, grapefruit, quince, gooseberry, with bracing minerality).
3_second_reach: Carl Loewen — farming the exact same Detzem vineyard their family bought from a secularized abbey in 1805. Two centuries, one site.

$title: Chateau de Rouanne Brut Nature Rose Organic 2021  750ml
$description: Château de Rouanne is a historic estate with a 12th century medieval castle, situated on a classified Roman site located in the southern Rhône Valley. The name of the estate comes from "Rugius", which is said to be the name of the original Roman owner. The estate totals 177 acres (72 hectares), including 153 acres (62 hectares) of vines. Château de Rouanne was purchased by Louis Barruol, owner and winemaker of Château de Saint Cosme, in May of 2019. Barruol sees enormous potential in Château de Rouanne, having worked with the previous owners for years as a source for some of his négociant wines. “It reminds me a lot of Saint Cosme when I took it over in 1992. It’s an unknown sleeping beauty waiting for a vigneron to truly love it.” The vineyard of Château de Rouanne is a unique one-block monopole, planted entirely with 50+ year old vines, which are a selection massale of Grenache, Syrah and Mourvèdre. The ancient terroir is comprised of limestone and sandy marl soils dating back to the Pliocene epoch. Harvested in the cool early morning hours, the grapes undergo a lengthy pressing followed by fermentation using indigenous yeasts in concrete vats to preserve the character and purity of the terroir. The second fermentation occurs with zero dosage. Clean, invigorating notes of silex on the nose showcase the limestone soils of the Rouanne vineyard. The aromas and flavors develop as the wines opens to reveal wild strawberry and fresh thyme – a complex and flavorful sparkling rosé. The tension of the acidity and bubbles lifts the rounds of the red fruit flavors, making this a fresh and elegant sparkling wine. It is an ideal aperitif and can be served with hors d'oeuvres, oysters, or a variety of charcuterie and light salads.
3_second_reach: Château de Rouanne — Louis Barruol of Château de Saint Cosme's Southern Rhône project. Certified organic, zero dosage, off a 12th-century estate.

$description: The Bründlmayer Kamptaler Terrassen Grüner Veltliner 2022 is a classic entry-level to mid-tier white wine from one of Austria's most respected producers in the Kamptal region. Weingut Bründlmayer, based in Langenlois, is renowned for high-quality Grüner Veltliner and Riesling from grand cru sites, with Willi Bründlmayer widely regarded as a top Austrian winemaker. This "Terrassen" bottling is a blend from various terraced vineyards (hence the name), often featuring stonier, schisted granite soils at higher elevations. It showcases the fresh, mineral-driven style typical of Kamptal Grüner Veltliner, with about 12.5% ABV and dry profile. Tasting Notes Appearance: Bright pale yellow-green with silver reflections. Aroma/Nose: Youthful and inviting, with pome fruit (green apple, pear), citrus (zest, lime), hay/acacia flowers, subtle herbal notes (meadow herbs, savory), and sometimes hints of mango/pineapple or slight yeasty freshness in youth. Palate: Medium-bodied, juicy, elegant, and crisp with lively acidity. Flavors include apple/pear, savory herbal overtones, white pepper, lentil/white pepper spice (classic Grüner signature), stone fruit, and mineral grip. Finishes firm, persistent, balanced, and refreshing. Overall Style: Vibrant, fresh, and versatile—balances vigor and elegance, with good complexity for an entry-level DAC wine.
3_second_reach: Bründlmayer — Willi Bründlmayer's Kamptal estate, one of the names Austria points to first for Grüner Veltliner.

$description: The Nikolaihof Vom Stein Smaragd Riesling 2017 is a highly regarded dry white wine from the Wachau region in Austria, produced by the renowned biodynamic winery Nikolaihof (Familie Saahs). Nikolaihof is one of the oldest and most respected estates in the Wachau, known for its meticulous, low-intervention approach and Demeter-certified biodynamic farming. "Vom Stein" refers to a specific sub-site (Ried Vom Stein) within the larger Silberbichl vineyard near Mautern—an east-sloping parcel with gneiss soils featuring mica inclusions, plus layers of loess and topsoil. This contributes to the wine's distinctive minerality and structure. "Smaragd" is the top quality designation in the Wachau for the ripest, most concentrated, and fullest-bodied wines (typically dry with higher alcohol and extract). Key Characteristics (2017 Vintage) Style: Dry (bone-dry or very close to it), full-bodied, elegant Riesling with pronounced minerality, texture, and aging potential. Color: Light to medium golden. Aromas & Flavors (from critic notes and tastings): Nose: Pure and refined, with bright ripe fruits (dried peach, waxy apple, mirabelle plum, nectarine), floral overtones, lemon peel/zest, subtle smokiness, saline/mineral notes, and hints of chamomile, herbs, or yeasty elements. Palate: Round, intense, and dense yet elegant; smooth and balm-like texture with cloud-like presence, stoniness, fine saline acidity, dried lemon, and a waxy/salty finish. Some describe it as earthy/savory with white chocolate, cider, or beeswax nuances. Overall: High finesse, persistent acidity, and complexity—approachable now but with excellent evolution. Critic Scores Wine Advocate (Stephan Reinhardt): 94 points — Praised for its pure, refined bouquet with bright ripe fruits, smoky/saline terroir, delicate oak influence; full-bodied, dense, elegant, with striking intensity and finesse (tasted 2022). Vinous: 94 points — Highlighted floral notes, dried peach, waxy apple, cloud-like texture, stoniness, dried lemon peel; smooth, bone-dry, salty/waxy finish (recent tastings).
3_second_reach: Nikolaihof — Austria's oldest winery, and the Wachau's original biodynamic believer. Smaragd means this is their ripest, richest pour.

$description: The Prieler Johanneshohe Blaufränkisch 2018 is a red wine from Weingut Prieler, a respected family winery in Burgenland, Austria. Blaufränkisch (also known as Lemberger or Kékfrankos) is the signature grape of the region, known for its elegant, peppery, and fruit-forward profile—often compared to a mix of Pinot Noir's finesse, Syrah's spice, and Cabernet Franc's freshness. This 2018 vintage comes from the Ried Johanneshohe vineyard (or parcels in the Schützen/Oggau area), featuring calcareous loam soils with elements like limestone and mica schist. The winemaking typically involves whole-berry fermentation (around 14 days) and aging in large oak casks (often 2–3 years in used barrels), emphasizing balance over heavy oak influence. The producer focuses on organic practices in many cases. Tasting Notes and Characteristics Appearance: Intense ruby red with purple reflections, fading to garnet/ochre at the rim. Aroma: Dark and ripe fruit-forward—black cherries, plums, blackberries, and blueberries, often with spicy-savory notes (pepper, cloves), hints of tar, earth, herbs, smoke, and baking spices. Palate: Medium to full-bodied, voluptuously ripe with juicy red and purple fruits, fine-grained tannins, vibrant acidity, and a fresh, mineral edge. It's well-balanced, velvety, and engaging, with a bright, lingering finish. Descriptions highlight elegance, drinkability, and an "airy" foundation despite depth and intensity. Style: Light-to-medium perfumed red, approachable yet with good structure and aging potential. Alcohol around 13%. Critics and users praise the 2018 for its freshness taming the dense fruit, making it seductive and classic.
3_second_reach: Prieler — Burgenland's benchmark for Blaufränkisch, the grape that built Austria's reputation for structured, peppery reds.

$title: Selbach Oster Wehlener Sonnenuhr Riesling Spatlese Mosel 2021 750ml
$description: The 2021 Selbach-Oster Wehlener Sonnenuhr Riesling Spätlese is a classic off-dry (feinfruchtig/fruity-sweet) Mosel Riesling from one of Germany's most legendary vineyards: Wehlener Sonnenuhr (Wehlen Sundial), a steep, slate-rich site along the Mosel River known for producing elegant, mineral-driven wines with great aging potential. Selbach-Oster is a highly regarded family estate in Zeltingen, with prime holdings in top sites like Wehlener Sonnenuhr and Zeltinger Sonnenuhr. This vintage (2021) was a cooler, high-acidity year in the Mosel, resulting in wines with freshness, precision, and balance despite the Spätlese level of ripeness (late harvest with some noble rot influence possible). Key Characteristics and Tasting Notes Critics and retailers consistently praise the 2021 for its stunning balance of richness and elegance: Aromas and flavors often feature a basket of yellow fruits — ripe peach, apricot, pear, nectarine, with hints of tropical notes (pineapple, melon) and citrus. It's described as lush, mouthfilling, and textured, with a creamy richness balanced by crystalline acidity and a salty, savory mineral edge (typical of slate soils). Low alcohol (around 8%) keeps it refreshing, not heavy. Finish is super-long, succulent, and finesse-driven, with integrated natural sweetness that's never cloying. Some notes highlight its juicy succulence, piquant freshness, and complexity that exceeds expectations for the category. Reviews call it "stunning," "beautiful," and highly drinkable young, but with clear potential to evolve over 10–20+ years.
3_second_reach: Selbach-Oster — old vines on the Mosel's single most famous slope, the one with an actual sundial carved into it: Wehlener Sonnenuhr.

$title: Von Winning Deidesheimer Paradiesgarten Riesling Trocken, Pfalz 2021 750ml
$description: The Von Winning Deidesheimer Paradiesgarten Riesling Trocken from the Pfalz region in Germany (2021 vintage) is a highly regarded dry (trocken) Riesling from one of the estate's top Erste Lage (Premier Cru) sites. Von Winning, a leading producer in the Pfalz, focuses on precise, terroir-driven dry Rieslings with meticulous vineyard work and barrel fermentation. The Paradiesgarten vineyard is a cooler, elegant site near the forest edge on loam and sandstone soils, contributing to finesse and minerality. Key Details Style: Dry white Riesling (Trocken), fermented spontaneously in 500L barrels and aged on lees for about 12 months, giving a silky texture with firm structure and length. Critic Scores: Often in the 90-point range (e.g., Wine Enthusiast rated the 2021 at 90 points). Price Range: Usually $35–$55 per bottle, depending on retailer. Tasting Notes This wine is elegant, juicy, and refined, with assertive acidity balancing the elements. Common aromas and flavors include: White and yellow stone fruits (peach, apricot, green apple) Citrus notes (lime zest, orange, grapefruit) Tropical hints (passionfruit, spice) Mineral/saline undertones, sometimes subtle petrol or white flowers A long, intense, salty-piquant finish with phenolic grip and finesse. It's described as round yet tight, with a stimulating mineral core—very refreshing and food-friendly.
3_second_reach: Von Winning — the Pfalz estate that reinvented dry German Riesling with barrel fermentation. This one's off the vineyard literally named 'paradise garden.'

$title: Von Winning Kirchenstuck Riesling Grosses Gewachs Pfalz 2021 750ml
$description: The 2021 Von Winning Kirchenstück Riesling Grosses Gewächs is a top-tier dry Riesling from the renowned Pfalz region in Germany. Weingut von Winning, based in Deidesheim, is highly regarded for producing some of Germany's finest dry Rieslings, with a focus on premier sites like this one. They emphasize low-intervention winemaking, including spontaneous fermentation in large oak barrels (500L) and extended lees aging (often 24 months on gross lees), which adds complexity, texture, and subtle oak influence without overpowering the fruit. Vineyard and Style Vineyard: Forster Kirchenstück — one of Germany's most prestigious and valuable sites (often called the most expensive vineyard in the country). Located in Forst an der Weinstraße, it's a small, walled parcel adjacent to the village church (hence "Kirchenstück"). The unique microclimate benefits from heat-retaining sandstone walls and airflow that keeps it dry and warm. Soils are complex: sandy clay, clay marl, loam, limestone rubble, and basalt, contributing minerality, power, and elegance. Style: This is a Grosses Gewächs (GG), the German equivalent of Grand Cru — dry, powerful, structured, and built for aging. Von Winning's versions tend to be full-bodied, rich, and dense, balancing intensity with finesse. Alcohol is typically around 13%. It's trocken (dry) but shows ripe fruit concentration from the warm Pfalz climate. Tasting Notes and Reviews (for the 2021 Vintage) The 2021 vintage in Pfalz was generally excellent for Riesling, with good acidity and balance. Specific notes on this wine include: Aromas of white peach, yellow apple, apricot, citrus (lemon/yellow citrus), pear, floral hints, currant leaf, and a mineral/saline base. Some reviews mention subtle tropical touches like pineapple or mango in riper expressions, plus gentle oak/smoke or vanilla influence from barrel aging. On the palate: Precise, elegant, and poised with vibrant acidity, richness, density, and a long, harmonious, saline-mineral finish. It's intense and powerful yet fine, with rejuvenating salinity and no excess drama. Full-bodied with a creamy texture, but balanced and not heavy. Critic/user impressions highlight its combination of power/finesse, minerality, and aging potential. It's often described as impressive, with great structure for cellaring.
3_second_reach: Von Winning — same estate that redefined dry German Riesling. Kirchenstück is a Grosses Gewächs, their highest single-vineyard tier.

$description: Faust Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon 2023 is a 100% Cabernet Sauvignon from the Faust winery (part of the Huneeus family, also behind Quintessa). It's a modern, polished Napa Valley Cab that emphasizes balance, freshness, and approachability while retaining structure for aging. Key Details Producer: Faust Wines, with winemaking by David Jelinek and estate direction by Jen Beloz. Vineyard Sources: Primarily from the Faust Estate Vineyard in Coombsville (a cooler, volcanic-soil AVA in southeastern Napa with marine influence, contributing minerality and freshness), supplemented by fruit from other Napa sites like Rutherford, Oakville, and Yountville. The Coombsville portion gives it a distinctive savory, structured edge. Winemaking: Aged 20 months in French oak (about 25% new). The 2023 vintage reflects a long, cool growing season in Napa, leading to good acidity, purity, lower alcohols (often under 15%), and elegant rather than overly ripe or jammy styles. Tasting Notes Winemaker and retailer descriptions highlight an elegantly structured and polished wine with excellent balance between freshness and richness. Aroma: Black currant, cassis, blackberry, red and dark fruits, with cool forest floor notes, oak spice, bay laurel, fragrant underbrush, star anise, crushed stones, dried herbs, flowers, and a savory/meaty undertone (salt-cured meat or tobacco). Some notes mention graphite or wet slate minerality. Palate: Concentrated flavors of Luxardo cherry, blueberry compote, dark cocoa, black cherry, and sometimes espresso or toasted spice. It has a silken/silky mouthfeel, fine-grained tannins, a succulent minerally finish, and a backbone of acidity that provides lift and length. It's described as tightly woven, broad yet velvety, with good nerve and approachability young, while having the structure to age. Style: Bold and powerful in the classic Napa sense but elegant and not over-extracted—think ripe fruit with savory complexity and polish rather than pure power. Early user notes on CellarTracker praise its plush texture, dark fruit, supple tannins, and aging potential (one 91-point note from early 2026). It pairs well with grilled or roasted red meats, aged cheeses, or hearty dishes where the fruit and structure can shine. Ratings and Vintage Context Specific critic scores for the 2023 Faust Napa Valley Cabernet (not the higher-end "The Pact" bottling) are still emerging, but early impressions align with the structured, fresh style of the 2023 Napa vintage overall. The cooler, extended season favored elegance and energy in Cabernets.
3_second_reach: 100% Cabernet Sauvignon from the Faust winery (part of the Huneeus family, also behind Quintessa).   Try this as a baby Quintessa.

$description: The Flowers Sonoma Coast Chardonnay 2024 is an elegant, cool-climate Chardonnay from Flowers Vineyard & Winery, sourced from organically farmed vineyards in the windy, coastal-influenced far Sonoma Coast AVA of California. This region imparts bright acidity, minerality, and a sense of place with Pacific influences like seaspray and salinity. Winemaking and Style Fermentation and Aging: 20% in stainless steel and 80% in French oak barrels (18% new, 62% 1-2 years old, 20% neutral 3+ years), followed by 16 months of barrel aging before bottling. This approach yields texture and subtle oak integration without heavy buttery or oaky notes—it's more Burgundian in style than many California Chardonnays. ABV: Typically around 13.5%. Profile: Bright, energetic, and lively with racy acidity, medium richness, and a finely woven, elegant texture. It emphasizes purity, precision, and coastal freshness rather than opulence. Tasting Notes Aromas: Soaring lemon cream, Meyer lemon, lemon zest, green apple, pear, white peach/apricot, tangerine oil, white flowers (jasmine), lemongrass, mint, white pepper, subtle beeswax, seaspray/briny minerality, and hints of wet stone or crushed almond. Some notes describe it as perfumed and forward due to the warmer 2024 season. Palate: Fresh citrus (lemon, lime, mandarin), orchard fruit (pear, white peach), pithy herbaceous notes, fine green citrus oil, and a mineral/saline backbone. The finish is long, focused, crisp yet textured, with mouthwatering acidity and clean minerality. It's described as vivid, tangy, and food-friendly. Professional Scores (early reviews): Antonio Galloni (Vinous): 91 — "A terrific introduction to the range... especially forward, open-knit Chardonnay." James Suckling: 94 Decanter: 93 It's often praised as expressive with great food-pairing potential (seafood, poultry, creamy cheeses, salads, or lighter dishes), and it should age gracefully for several years thanks to its acidity and balance.
3_second_reach: Flowers — one of the original pioneers of the extreme Sonoma Coast. Camp Meeting Ridge fog is what gives this Chardonnay its edge.

$description: The domaine traces to the 1930s, when Fernand Pernot began acquiring Gevrey-Chambertin vineyards; his nephew Jean-Claude Fourrier took over in the late 1960s and expanded into Chambolle, Morey, and Vougeot.
